speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To help narrow down the cause, can you describe the nature of your abdominal pain and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms are significant, particularly the combination of weight loss and night sweats. I need to examine the lymph node and your abdomen; does the node feel hard or rubbery, and is it tender to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: A fixed, non-tender supraclavicular node is a concerning sign for malignancy. I will request a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis to look for a primary tumor. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the massively enlarged lymph nodes and your B-symptoms, we need to confirm the cell type involved. REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cervical Lymph Node Biopsy: Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms a B-cell lineage with high proliferation, strongly suggesting an aggressive Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma such as Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
